description:
Canonical ACCORDION layout-parity scenario for the four panes (fleet status, task list, holding area, epic board). Sibling of notifications-parity-scenario.json, which covers the notifications surface and is NOT extended by this file. Feeds the inner-accordion contract rows added to LAYOUT-CONTRACT.md at 610ba797.

THIS FIXTURE IS NOT THE CONTRACT. It is an INPUT chosen to exercise the contract rows in LAYOUT-CONTRACT.md. If the two ever disagree, THE CONTRACT ROWS WIN and this file is the thing that gets corrected — a fixture that outranks its contract is how today's rendering quietly becomes tomorrow's specification.

SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE FILER LABEL IS LEGACY, NOT THE MUX. notifications.js:9889 _taskFilerLabel is the spec; multiplexer/render/holdingAreaModel.ts taskFilerLabel reproduces it. Legacy's own Ensures block enumerates the cases this fixture covers: 'mr radio 0e61abe3' -> 'Mr Radio'; 'Krishna 420f5ec9' -> 'Krishna'; no trailing session id -> the whole string, display-cased; absent/blank -> the em dash. Case is DISPLAY-ONLY - the store holds 'Krishna' and 'mr radio' both.

created_by VALUES ARE REALISTIC ON PURPOSE - '<persona> <8-hex session>'. An earlier cut of this fixture used bare 'maria'/'rick', which exercises only the no-session-id fall-through and never the TWO-WORD PERSONA that legacy's docstring records as wrong on 6 of 13 live rows under a leading-word implementation. A fixture in a shape the real data does not have cannot see the defect the code was written against.

GROUP SIZES ARE DELIBERATELY DISTINCT - owners 4/2/1, epics 3/2/1, filers 3/2/1. Equal sizes are interchangeable in the data, so a swap between two groupings would be invisible however the assertions are named.

OWNER AND EPIC GROUPINGS CROSS-CUT ON PURPOSE - alice's rows span alpha, beta and drift, so a walker that confuses the two groupings gets a different answer rather than a coincidentally equal one.

a1000007 CARRIES NO correlation_key AT ALL and is DRIFT, not a group: epicKeyOf() returns null for it and the model's contract says drift is 'never silently dropped'. b2000005 carries the literal key 'epic:unassigned', which IS a group and sorts LAST. The two are different states and a fixture with only one of them cannot tell a walker that confuses them from one that does not.

EPIC_STORIES IS A MAP OF {title, story} OBJECTS, NOT OF BARE STRINGS. An earlier cut of this fixture mapped 'epic:alpha' to a plain string. The mux reads story.story (epicBoardModel.ts epicStoryText), so a string yields "" and NO tr.epic-story-row renders at all - the contract row would have been exercised by nothing while the fixture appeared to cover it. The shape is confirmed against the real hand-maintained input, src/conf/epic-stories.json, whose every entry is {"title": ..., "story": ...}. epic:beta deliberately carries NO entry, so the storied and story-less cases are both real.

tasks.title: Drift - carries no epic key at all

epic:alpha.title: Alpha
epic:alpha.story: Alpha exists to prove the story row renders inside the group.
